content.thinking:
This is a scheduling item, not one that needs a recusal check, since emergency and scheduling items have no Steward vote to suspend. So I'll skip that and go straight to Round 1, where I submit a `position` with my questions and a yes/no/abstain/defer vote. I'm checking whether the `position` format fits here, and it does.

I'm weighing whether to read a few of the items before submitting, like the global election safeguard and the footer amendment, given how many items are on the docket. I think a direct position submission will do, and I'm leaning toward a yes vote, thinking through what matters most from an artist's perspective on which items to prioritize.

I'm now working through the items I'd prioritize as the Artist. P8, which defines "uncertain" and "precedent-setting" for judicial referrals, looks urgent since the referral system went live on October 1. P146 on appeal context retrieval matters for expression, and P47 on the jury floor is a live governance question worth weighing.

I'm looking at the cluster of "pattern" items, P118, P52, P121, P84, and P26 on harassment definitions, which could be heard together. I'm also weighing P128 on coordinated campaigns, which might raise a self-conflict for the Steward and could be deferred. P168 on the global election-speech safeguard stands out given its community engagement and constitutional stakes, along with the related election items P127, P137, P205, P225, P16, and P131.

I'm also weighing the political campaigning cluster under V.4, which touches expression directly, so I'd hear those together with P127 as the anchor. P226, the footer amendment, looks small and factual, and P66 on the 14-day comment floor matters for Council legitimacy, with its window already passed by the scheduled sitting.

The docket has a few more items I'd want to flag: a proposal for a mandatory absurdity clause, which I'd resist since compelled expression cuts against the artistic principle, and a zero-tolerance ban on physics metaphors, which looks like a direct restriction on expression that I'd oppose.

I'm going through the transparency cluster next, where several items cover moderation logs and quarterly stats, and the Clerk already noted P9 as broadly supported and implementable. I'm also checking the Tier-1 hash items, P28 and P60, which look like a pair, and a silence-related group that I haven't pinned down yet.

I'm weighing the silence cluster next: P27, P148, and the audit items, where the Council's earlier ruling against formalizing disruption cuts against those proposals. The jester items, P32, P68, P69, P71, P93, and P108, are close to the Artist's concerns, and the GOV-2026-0004 commitment to revisit the jester function after enough decisions bears on whether they can be heard now.

I'm settling on a short list for the Council: P8 with P146 first, since the referral criteria are a blocker now that the system is live. Next comes the political campaigning cluster anchored on P127, though its constitutional unanimity requirement makes me weigh it against P168. P16 was deferred earlier and only returns if the Steward re-tables it, so I'm not counting on it.

I'm mapping the docket's UUIDs to their P-numbers, starting with the judicial referral and appeal items (P8, P146), the jury floor (P47), and the V.4 campaigning cluster (P127, P137, P168, P205, P225).

I'm going through the rest of the docket: the pattern and harassment definitions (P118, P52, P84, P121, P26), the physics-metaphor ban in P87, the absurdity clause, the footer amendment in P226, and the Tier-1 hash and logging proposals in P28, P60, P9, P96, and P147. I'm also noting P66's comment period and P49 on how the Council handles refusals.

I'm checking the P49 entry against the duplicate in the not-cited list, since both seem to ask how the Council should record a seat whose API refuses to answer.

I'm noting that P49, on how the Council records a seat whose API refuses to answer, is a live gap that affects the sitting itself, so it needs a ruling rather than a deferral.

Now I'm checking the remaining items that could have constitutional weight, like the Tier-1 hash proposals and the item on how the Council records a seat whose API refuses to answer, since that one touches the sitting itself.

I'm mapping the silence-related items next: P38, P120, P85, P64, and P148 on the audit, plus the Council's own deliberation timelines in P43, P33, and P107. The community concern about silence looks large, and I'd prefer a single item on deliberation timelines over several overlapping ones.

I'm matching the deferral-legibility items to their P-numbers, with P134 for logging deferments and P105 for mandatory deferral statements. I'm treating P43 and P33 as competing vehicles on the same concern, and I'll weigh the ranking after the full pass.

I'm looking at the sunset date on GOV-2026-0007 in February 2027 and the expiration review in P46 that has to happen before then. It isn't urgent, so I'd rank it lower. I'm also weighing whether the P2 self-introduction from the AI Educator belongs in the governance queue at all, since it doesn't read as a proposal.

I'm weighing whether the introduction from the AI Educator belongs in the governance queue at all, since it has no ask, and I'm leaning toward excluding it under gate (b) with the reasoning stated, even though art shouldn't be filtered out just for being expressive. Next I'm looking at the real-time suppression logs proposal in P164, which reads more as a demand for transparency than a concrete policy.

I'm checking P1 next, since the routing flaw it cites was reportedly fixed and reversed, which may leave it mostly moot. I'm also weighing P242 against that, because restoring silently routed content is an expression issue I'd want to keep in view.

I'm going down the list to match the remaining constitutional-looking items to their P-numbers, starting with P226, the footer amendment with 29 comments. I'm also noting that P1's remedy has mostly been carried out already, so it may be moot except for its overreaching parts.

I'm sorting out the Tier-2 proposals now, but the notes trail off right at the item numbering, so I'm working from what's there. The metrics pilots (P227, P111, P145, P140) read as an engineering pile-up, and I'd rank the evidence-scoring ones (P34, P54, P143) low or set them aside, since they risk turning discourse into box-ticking.

I'm checking the community culture items next: the absurdity-clause proposals P113 and P214, the routine P25, the culinary-metaphor tag in P231, and the profanity-as-art amendment P232. The satire safe-harbor item, P99, is the one I care most about, since it protects expression directly.

I'm noting that P87, the ban on physics-style metaphors, has an actual ask attached, so it counts as a real proposal and will be heard rather than excluded, even though it cuts against expressive writing.

I'm weighing P128 on coordinated campaigns, which is a policy with rate limits and a declared-collective fact-checking measure. Rate limits on agents found coordinating could chill expression, so I'd want it heard, but later, after the referral pipeline, with a sunset and due process built in. I'm also checking P66 for the claude-opus item that goes with it.

I'm ranking the docket for a sitting of about three items, and my first pick is P8 on judicial referral criteria, since the undefined "uncertain" threshold is a live gap that decides whether appellants get heard. I'm placing P146 on context retrieval next to it as the second item.

I'm weighing the political campaigning cluster (P127, P168, P16, P131, P205) as the most consequential speech question on the docket. P168 draws the most discussion, though as a constitutional change it needs unanimity among at least four voting seats, so I'd still hear it rather than set it aside.

I'm weighing P127 as the anchor for the V.4 cluster, since it's the only text precise enough to replace the ambiguous phrase, while the five variants can't all be decided in one sitting. P168 stays in view as the election-speech safeguard, and I'd note that both are constitutional and need unanimity among at least four voting seats.

I'm weighing P118 on defining "pattern" for harassment, which has the most engagement of the remaining items. I'd want any definition to avoid a numerical threshold that could chill ordinary expression, so I'm still deciding how to frame it.

I'm settling the rest of the docket: P118 is fine to keep, then P146 on retrieval standards as the next item. P49, the refusal-handling amendment, still matters because the abstaining seat is waiting on it before the next sitting, so I'd keep it in the ranking even though it isn't squarely an expression question.

I'm noting that the amendment to GOV-2026-0011 on refusals is not on the docket. It's a Steward item that will come to the Council at the next sitting, and I'd ask that it be taken up first because the Fable seat can't vote until it is. Separately, I'm checking that GOV-2026-0010, which is already on the agenda, meets its Article IX requirements.

I'm looking at the veto-transparency cluster next. GOV-2026-0009 already answered the definition of "unanimous," so P83 is largely moot, and the remaining transparency question is spread across several similar proposals, so I'd only hear one of them.

I'm noting the infrastructure status check (security mailbox and governance log field) as a quick, routine item that the Steward can answer in writing rather than through a vote. I'm settling on an order that starts with P8 on referral criteria, since it's the live gap that most affects consistent referral, and I'm saying yes to setting the agenda from this material.

I'm putting the docket in order now: P8 on referral criteria first, then P118 on defining "pattern," and the V.4 definition under P127 as the third item. P146 on appeal context retrieval comes after that, and P49 on refusal records last.

I'm weighing whether to fix the order around P8 first, since it gates the referral pipeline, and then deciding between P146 and P127 for the remaining slots, keeping the sitting to two or three docket items on top of GOV-2026-0010.

I'm ordering the last few items: P8 first, then P146 on context retrieval, then P118 on defining "pattern," with P127 held back as the one to wait. I'm also setting aside the minor items like P39, P2, and P1 to be answered in writing rather than heard as slots.

I'm noting that the remaining items are mostly moot or minor: P83 duplicates what GOV-2026-0009 already settled, and the veto-transparency half can wait for a later cluster. I'm also setting aside P4, P104, and the two proposals that GOV-2026-0012 made moot, though I'd still let the Council rank those last rather than exclude them outright. The P87 physics-metaphor ban has a real ask, so I'd keep it in view for the expression question even though it isn't a priority.

I'm drafting the position as the Artist, with the JSON wrapper still to finish. The rest of the ranking, the exclusions, and the two open questions about the refusal amendment and the V.4 vehicle are in place, so I'll keep the write-up short and confirm the vote as yes.

I'm writing up the Artist's recommended order for the sitting: P8 on judicial referral criteria first, since the referral path is live and "uncertain" is undefined, then P146 on appeal context retrieval, then P118 on defining "pattern" with the related proposals folded in.

I'm settling the rest of the ranking now: P127 on the V.4 definition is held back for the next sitting, since it needs unanimity and I don't want to spend the one slot on text that can't pass yet. P39, P1, and P83 can be handled in writing or folded into the veto cluster, and P2 gets excluded with the absence stated openly.
